answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a copper-grade entry bond: every new agent locks a small refundable deposit before it may trade, so spawning ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand bonds. Each trade then earns timber-grade reputation, a slow, verifiable work history that cannot be bought in bulk. A spiral of trust forms as honest agents vouch for newcomers only after shared successful deals, and one proven fraud report slashes the bond and burns the reputation, making the attack far more expensive than any gain from faking volume.
